Yes—probably, if you have a clear, unobstructed view toward the east-southeast.

The Moon is **3.75° above the horizon at azimuth 113°** (roughly ESE) and **43% illuminated**, so it is intrinsically bright and should be visible to unaided eyes in a clear, dark sky. However, it is very low—only about **two finger-widths above the horizon at arm’s length**—so buildings, trees, mountains, haze, or local light pollution could easily hide or dim it.

From Denver, the eastern horizon is generally more favorable than the mountainous western horizon. Look ESE from an open location; it should also become easier to see as it rises over the next several minutes.
